37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. STRATEGY FILE
41: 
42: `deep-research-strategy.md` is the persistent research plan. The reducer owns machine-managed sections.
43: 
44: Required sections:
45: 
46: - Research Topic
47: - Known Context
48: - Key Questions
49: - Answered Questions
50: - What Worked
51: - What Failed
52: - Exhausted Approaches
53: - Ruled-Out Directions
54: - Next Focus
55: 
56: Update protocol:
57: 
58: - read strategy before each iteration;
59: - choose one focus from `Next Focus`;
60: - append what worked, failed, and was ruled out;
61: - update answered/open questions through reducer-owned sections;
62: - when a STOP candidate is blocked, override `Next Focus` with the blocker recovery focus.
63: 
64: ---
65: 
66: ## 3. ITERATION FILES
67: 
68: Iteration files are write-once markdown narratives.
69: 
70: ```text
71: research/iterations/iteration-001.md
72: research/iterations/iteration-002.md
73: research/iterations/iteration-003.md
74: ```
75: 
76: Required shape:
77: 
78: | Markdown Element | Required Content |
79: |------------------|------------------|
80: | H1 title | `Iteration N: Focus Area` |
81: | `Focus` section | What this iteration investigated |
82: | `Findings` section | Evidence-backed findings with source citations |
83: | `Sources Consulted` section | Files, URLs, memory hits, or commands used |
84: | `Assessment` section | `newInfoRatio`, novelty justification, and confidence notes |
85: | `Reflection` section | What worked, failed, or was ruled out |
86: | `Recommended Next Focus` section | One concrete next focus |
87: 
88: Every finding must cite a source such as `[SOURCE: file:path:line]` or `[SOURCE: https://example.test]`.
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 4. RESEARCH SYNTHESIS
93: 
94: `research.md` is the workflow-owned synthesis output at `{artifact_dir}/research.md`.
95: 
96: Rules:
97: 
98: - progressive synthesis may update the file during the loop;
99: - final synthesis consolidates duplicate findings and unresolved gaps;
100: - prior findings are not silently overwritten;
101: - generated or machine-owned sections must be marked explicitly when the workflow uses them;
102: - when `resource_map_present` is true, cite `{spec_folder}/resource-map.md` in References.
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. DASHBOARD
107: 
108: `deep-research-dashboard.md` is auto-generated from JSONL, strategy, and registry state.
109: 
110: Expected sections:
111: 
112: | Section | Source |
113: |---------|--------|
114: | Iteration Table | JSONL iteration records |
115: | Question Status | Strategy + registry |
116: | Convergence Trend | `convergenceSignals` + reducer |
117: | Dead Ends | JSONL `ruledOut` + strategy |
118: | Blocked Stops | Registry blocked-stop history |
119: | Graph Convergence | Graph convergence registry fields |
120: | Next Focus | Strategy |
121: 
122: Generation rules:
123: 
124: - regenerate after each iteration evaluation;
125: - compute derived values from raw state;
126: - overwrite the full dashboard rather than appending;
127: - if state is missing, write a minimal "No iteration data available" dashboard;
128: - agent writes are discarded on next refresh.
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## 6. RESOURCE MAP
133: 
134: When `{spec_folder}/resource-map.md` exists at init:
135: 
136: - persist `resource_map_present: true` in config;
137: - summarize section counts and themes into strategy `Known Context`;
138: - treat listed files as known inventory, not net-new discoveries;
139: - cite the map in final synthesis references;
140: - emit `{artifact_dir}/resource-map.md` from converged deltas unless disabled.
141: 
142: When absent:
143: 
144: - persist `resource_map_present: false`;
145: - write `resource-map.md not present; skipping coverage gate` into `Known Context`;
146: - continue normally.
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## 7. SPEC ANCHORING OUTPUT
151: 
152: `references/protocol/spec-check-protocol.md` defines bounded `spec.md` writes:
153: 
154: - acquire `research/.deep-research.lock`;
155: - classify `folder_state`;
156: - seed or append bounded context during init when allowed;
157: - replace exactly one generated findings fence during synthesis.
158: 
159: This output path is protocol-owned, not iteration-agent owned.

16: # Deep Research JSONL State Reference
17: 
18: `deep-research-state.jsonl` is append-only. Each line is one JSON object. The first line is normally the config record, followed by iteration and event records.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Define the append-only JSONL records used by deep-research config, iteration, lifecycle, graph, pause, stuck-recovery, and blocked-stop state.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: Load this reference when validating state logs, adding event records, reconstructing a packet, or mapping legacy stop labels to current values.
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: Raw JSONL is append-only evidence. Reducer-owned files derive from it, but they do not replace it.
35: 
36: ### How Records Get Written
37: 
38: Canonical records are written by calling the append gateway, not by writing to the file:
39: 
40: ```bash
41: node .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/append-mode-event.cjs \
42:   --mode research \
43:   --run-directory <spec folder> \
44:   --event-json <path to one JSON record>
45: ```
46: 
47: The gateway authorizes the write against the mode's durable authority record, serialises it behind
48: the ledger fence, returns a receipt, and refreshes this file from the ledger. Exit `0` means the
49: record is durable; exit `2` means it was refused and the refusal names the check that failed.
50: 
51: Writing to `deep-research-state.jsonl` directly bypasses all four of those properties. Two writers
52: with no shared ordering can interleave, and a record nobody authorized carries no receipt, so a
53: later reader cannot tell an accepted record from an invented one. The file below remains the
54: readable surface — six consumers depend on it — but under ledger authority it is a projection of the
55: ledger rather than the place writes land.
56: 
57: That split is authority-dependent: while the mode's authority record still names the legacy writer
58: (`authority-deep-research.json`, state `legacy_authoritative`), this file is the authoritative target
59: and no ledger backs it; the projection relationship begins when the record moves to
60: `new_authoritative_reversible` or `new_authoritative_final` with `selectedWriter: "dark"`. The
61: registered stems and their producer census live in `state-format.md` section 7, and
62: `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` fails when the
63: census and the emitter surface on disk disagree.
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 2. CONFIG RECORD
68: 
69: The config record captures the initialized loop contract.
70: 
71: ```json
72: {
73:   "type": "config",
74:   "topic": "API response time optimization",
75:   "maxIterations": 10,
76:   "convergenceThreshold": 0.05,
77:   "stuckThreshold": 3,
78:   "specFolder": "028-auto-deep-research",
79:   "createdAt": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
80: }
81: ```
82: 
83: The full config file also stores executor, lineage, reducer, capability matrix, pause sentinel, archive, and file-protection settings.
84: 
85: A ledger projection rebuilds this row thin — only `type`, `topic`, `maxIterations`, `generation`, and `timestamp` — so a refresh that would replace the row while dropping keys from an existing `type: "config"` first line is refused (`ATTRIBUTION_COLLAPSE`) rather than published. Move or migrate the legacy row deliberately before cutting the mode over.
86: 
87: A legacy config row sent through the gateway must carry `generation` and `maxIterations` as non-negative whole numbers, `topic` as a string and `executor` as a string or an object. A count written as a plain digit string such as `"10"` is carried as that number with a warning. Any other wrongly typed field is refused with `run-initialized-fields-mistyped:<field>`, so fix that field in the row and send it again.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## 3. ITERATION RECORDS
92: 
93: ```json
94: {
95:   "type": "iteration",
96:   "iteration": 1,
97:   "status": "complete",
98:   "focus": "Initial broad survey",
99:   "findingsCount": 5,
100:   "newInfoRatio": 1.0,
101:   "noveltyJustification": "First pass; all findings are new to this packet",
102:   "keyQuestions": ["What causes latency?"],
103:   "answeredQuestions": ["What causes latency?"],
104:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:05:00Z",
105:   "durationMs": 45000
106: }
107: ```
108: 
109: | Field | Required | Notes |
110: |-------|----------|-------|
111: | `type` | Yes | `iteration` |
112: | `iteration` | Yes | 1-indexed iteration number. The fan-out stop-policy validator reads only this field |
113: | `run` | Legacy | Older name for `iteration`. Readers still accept it; new records write `iteration` |
114: | `status` | Yes | See status values below |
115: | `focus` | Yes | Single focus investigated |
116: | `findingsCount` | Yes | Number of findings reported |
117: | `newInfoRatio` | Yes | Novelty score used by convergence |
118: | `noveltyJustification` | Recommended | One-sentence explanation of the ratio |
119: | `keyQuestions` | Recommended | Questions considered during this iteration |
120: | `answeredQuestions` | Recommended | Questions answered by evidence |
121: | `ruledOut` | Optional | Negative knowledge entries |
122: | `graphEvents` | Optional | Coverage graph mutations |
123: 
124: Event records in §7 keep their own `run` field, which names the iteration the event occurred in.
125: 
126: Status values:
127: 
128: | Status | Meaning |
129: |--------|---------|
130: | `complete` | Normal evidence-gathering iteration |
131: | `timeout` | Time/tool budget exceeded |
132: | `error` | Tool, parse, or unexpected failure |
133: | `stuck` | No new information and no clear next direction |
134: | `insight` | Low ratio but important conceptual breakthrough |
135: | `thought` | Analytical-only iteration; excluded from stuck and signal math |
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 4. CONVERGENCE SIGNAL FIELDS
140: 
141: When the composite algorithm runs, the iteration may include signal values:
142: 
143: ```json
144: {
145:   "type": "iteration",
146:   "iteration": 5,
147:   "convergenceSignals": {
148:     "rollingAvg": 0.12,
149:     "madScore": 0.08,
150:     "entropyCoverage": 0.71,
151:     "compositeStop": 0.42
152:   }
153: }
154: ```
155: 
156: Signal rules live in `../convergence/convergence-signals.md`.
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: ## 5. NEGATIVE KNOWLEDGE
161: 
162: Use `ruledOut` to preserve eliminated approaches.
163: 
164: ```json
165: {
166:   "type": "iteration",
167:   "iteration": 3,
168:   "status": "complete",
169:   "ruledOut": [
170:     {
171:       "approach": "HTTP/3 multiplexing",
172:       "reason": "No server-side support in target environment",
173:       "evidence": "file:docs/protocols.md:42"
174:     }
175:   ]
176: }
177: ```
178: 
179: Ruled-out directions should also appear in strategy and synthesis outputs.
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## 6. GRAPH EVENTS
184: 
185: `graphEvents` records coverage graph mutations from an iteration.
186: 
187: ```json
188: {
189:   "type": "iteration",
190:   "iteration": 4,
191:   "graphEvents": [
192:     {"type": "question", "id": "q-reconnect", "label": "How should reconnect work?"},
193:     {"type": "finding", "id": "f-backoff", "label": "Exponential backoff is required"},
194:     {"type": "edge", "from": "f-backoff", "to": "q-reconnect", "relation": "ANSWERS"}
195:   ]
196: }
197: ```
198: 
199: Valid node types are `question`, `finding`, `claim`, and `source`; `edge` records connect nodes. IDs must be unique within a single `(specFolder, loopType, sessionId)` namespace. Reusing the same logical ID across independent sessions is allowed because the coverage graph uses a composite key.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 7. EVENT RECORDS
204: 
205: Lifecycle event:
206: 
207: ```json
208: {
209:   "type": "event",
210:   "event": "resumed",
211:   "mode": "research",
212:   "sessionId": "dr-2026-05-24T00-00-00Z",
213:   "parentSessionId": "dr-2026-05-24T00-00-00Z",
214:   "lineageMode": "resume",
215:   "continuedFromRun": 4,
216:   "generation": 1,
217:   "archivedPath": null,
218:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
219: }
220: ```
221: 
222: Blocked stop event:
223: 
224: ```json
225: {
226:   "type": "event",
227:   "event": "blocked_stop",
228:   "mode": "research",
229:   "run": 7,
230:   "stopReason": "blockedStop",
231:   "blockedBy": ["keyQuestionCoverage", "sourceDiversity"],
232:   "recoveryStrategy": "focus_pivot",
233:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
234: }
235: ```
236: 
237: Pause event:
238: 
239: ```json
240: {
241:   "type": "event",
242:   "event": "userPaused",
243:   "mode": "research",
244:   "run": 7,
245:   "stopReason": "userPaused",
246:   "sentinelPath": "research/.deep-research-pause",
247:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
248: }
249: ```
250: 
251: Stuck recovery event:
252: 
253: ```json
254: {
255:   "type": "event",
256:   "event": "stuckRecovery",
257:   "mode": "research",
258:   "run": 7,
259:   "stopReason": "stuckRecovery",
260:   "fromFocus": "Connection pooling",
261:   "toFocus": "Transport alternatives",
262:   "strategy": "try_opposites",
263:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: Idea observation event:
268: 
269: ```json
270: {
271:   "type": "event",
272:   "event": "idea_observed",
273:   "mode": "research",
274:   "run": 7,
275:   "ideaId": "idea-cache-stampede",
276:   "idea": "Investigate cache stampede mitigation as a follow-up focus",
277:   "category": "ideas",
278:   "source": "iteration-007.md",
279:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
280: }
281: ```
282: 
283: Leaf agents may record `idea_observed` through the gateway for promising tangents. They must not record `idea_promoted`; promotion is reducer-owned.
284: 
285: Idea promotion event:
286: 
287: ```json
288: {
289:   "type": "event",
290:   "event": "idea_promoted",
291:   "mode": "research",
292:   "run": 8,
293:   "ideaId": "idea-cache-stampede",
294:   "idea": "Investigate cache stampede mitigation as a follow-up focus",
295:   "category": "ideas",
296:   "observationCount": 2,
297:   "minIdeaObservations": 2,
298:   "firstObservedRun": 6,
299:   "lastObservedRun": 7,
300:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:02:00Z"
301: }
302: ```
303: 
304: The reducer emits `idea_promoted` once per idea after replay shows `observationCount >= minIdeaObservations`. `minIdeaObservations` defaults to `2` and is clamped to the inclusive range `1..10`.
305: 
306: Rejected idea event:
307: 
308: ```json
309: {
310:   "type": "event",
311:   "event": "idea_rejected",
312:   "mode": "research",
313:   "run": 7,
314:   "ideaId": "idea-cache-stampede",
315:   "idea": "Investigate cache stampede mitigation as a follow-up focus",
316:   "category": "ideas",
317:   "reason": "Already rejected by environment evidence",
318:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
319: }
320: ```
321: 
322: `idea_rejected` durably suppresses the matching promoted idea and also enters the reducer-owned rejected-pattern cache. Use `category: "general"` only when the rejection should suppress matching text across next-focus, recovery, and ideas candidates.
323: 
324: Rejected idea removal event:
325: 
326: ```json
327: {
328:   "type": "event",
329:   "event": "idea_rejected_removed",
330:   "mode": "research",
331:   "pattern": "Retry HTTP/3 as the primary latency fix",
332:   "category": "next-focus",
333:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
334: }
335: ```
336: 
337: Rejected idea reset event:
338: 
339: ```json
340: {
341:   "type": "event",
342:   "event": "idea_rejected_reset",
343:   "mode": "research",
344:   "reason": "Operator wants previously rejected ideas eligible again",
345:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
346: }

16: # Deep Research JSONL State Reference
17: 
18: `deep-research-state.jsonl` is append-only. Each line is one JSON object. The first line is normally the config record, followed by iteration and event records.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Define the append-only JSONL records used by deep-research config, iteration, lifecycle, graph, pause, stuck-recovery, and blocked-stop state.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: Load this reference when validating state logs, adding event records, reconstructing a packet, or mapping legacy stop labels to current values.
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: Raw JSONL is append-only evidence. Reducer-owned files derive from it, but they do not replace it.
35: 
36: ### How Records Get Written
37: 
38: Canonical records are written by calling the append gateway, not by writing to the file:
39: 
40: ```bash
41: node .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/append-mode-event.cjs \
42:   --mode research \
43:   --run-directory <spec folder> \
44:   --event-json <path to one JSON record>
45: ```
46: 
47: The gateway authorizes the write against the mode's durable authority record, serialises it behind
48: the ledger fence, returns a receipt, and refreshes this file from the ledger. Exit `0` means the
49: record is durable; exit `2` means it was refused and the refusal names the check that failed.
50: 
51: Writing to `deep-research-state.jsonl` directly bypasses all four of those properties. Two writers
52: with no shared ordering can interleave, and a record nobody authorized carries no receipt, so a
53: later reader cannot tell an accepted record from an invented one. The file below remains the
54: readable surface — six consumers depend on it — but under ledger authority it is a projection of the
55: ledger rather than the place writes land.
56: 
57: That split is authority-dependent: while the mode's authority record still names the legacy writer
58: (`authority-deep-research.json`, state `legacy_authoritative`), this file is the authoritative target
59: and no ledger backs it; the projection relationship begins when the record moves to
60: `new_authoritative_reversible` or `new_authoritative_final` with `selectedWriter: "dark"`. The
61: registered stems and their producer census live in `state-format.md` section 7, and
62: `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` fails when the
63: census and the emitter surface on disk disagree.
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 2. CONFIG RECORD
68: 
69: The config record captures the initialized loop contract.
70: 
71: ```json
72: {
73:   "type": "config",
74:   "topic": "API response time optimization",
75:   "maxIterations": 10,
76:   "convergenceThreshold": 0.05,
77:   "stuckThreshold": 3,
78:   "specFolder": "028-auto-deep-research",
79:   "createdAt": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
80: }
81: ```
82: 
83: The full config file also stores executor, lineage, reducer, capability matrix, pause sentinel, archive, and file-protection settings.
84: 
85: A ledger projection rebuilds this row thin — only `type`, `topic`, `maxIterations`, `generation`, and `timestamp` — so a refresh that would replace the row while dropping keys from an existing `type: "config"` first line is refused (`ATTRIBUTION_COLLAPSE`) rather than published. Move or migrate the legacy row deliberately before cutting the mode over.
86: 
87: A legacy config row sent through the gateway must carry `generation` and `maxIterations` as non-negative whole numbers, `topic` as a string and `executor` as a string or an object. A count written as a plain digit string such as `"10"` is carried as that number with a warning. Any other wrongly typed field is refused with `run-initialized-fields-mistyped:<field>`, so fix that field in the row and send it again.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## 3. ITERATION RECORDS
92: 
93: ```json
94: {
95:   "type": "iteration",
96:   "iteration": 1,
97:   "status": "complete",
98:   "focus": "Initial broad survey",
99:   "findingsCount": 5,
100:   "newInfoRatio": 1.0,
101:   "noveltyJustification": "First pass; all findings are new to this packet",
102:   "keyQuestions": ["What causes latency?"],
103:   "answeredQuestions": ["What causes latency?"],
104:   "timestamp": "2026-05-24T00:05:00Z",
105:   "durationMs": 45000
106: }
107: ```
108: 
109: | Field | Required | Notes |
110: |-------|----------|-------|
111: | `type` | Yes | `iteration` |
112: | `iteration` | Yes | 1-indexed iteration number. The fan-out stop-policy validator reads only this field |
113: | `run` | Legacy | Older name for `iteration`. Readers still accept it; new records write `iteration` |
114: | `status` | Yes | See status values below |
115: | `focus` | Yes | Single focus investigated |
116: | `findingsCount` | Yes | Number of findings reported |
117: | `newInfoRatio` | Yes | Novelty score used by convergence |
118: | `noveltyJustification` | Recommended | One-sentence explanation of the ratio |
119: | `keyQuestions` | Recommended | Questions considered during this iteration |
120: | `answeredQuestions` | Recommended | Questions answered by evidence |
121: | `ruledOut` | Optional | Negative knowledge entries |
122: | `graphEvents` | Optional | Coverage graph mutations |

129: |--------|---------|
130: | `complete` | Normal evidence-gathering iteration |
131: | `timeout` | Time/tool budget exceeded |
132: | `error` | Tool, parse, or unexpected failure |
133: | `stuck` | No new information and no clear next direction |
134: | `insight` | Low ratio but important conceptual breakthrough |
135: | `thought` | Analytical-only iteration; excluded from stuck and signal math |

146:   "iteration": 5,

17: 
18: The reducer turns append-only iteration state into synchronized strategy, registry, dashboard, and synthesis metadata. It is the source of truth for derived packet state.

20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Define reducer ownership, findings registry shape, validation behavior, fault tolerance, file protection, dashboard derivation, and legacy aliases.

28: ### When to Use

31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: The reducer owns derived state. Manual edits to reducer-managed outputs are temporary and may be overwritten.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. REDUCER CONTRACT
39: 
40: The workflow reducer:
41: 
42: - reads `deep-research-state.jsonl`, per-iteration deltas, strategy, and iteration markdown;
43: - reads `inbox.jsonl` as immutable question input;
44: - reads the prior registry as canonical question state when present;
45: - validates required iteration artifacts;
46: - updates machine-owned strategy sections;
47: - regenerates the findings registry;
48: - regenerates the dashboard;
49: - records convergence and blocked-stop summaries.
50: 
51: It must fail closed before writing derived files when JSONL corruption is detected in strict mode.
52: 
53: Under ledger authority the JSONL it reads is a projection of the ledger, bounded by the registered stems; the registered vocabulary and the producer census are in `state-format.md` section 7, and `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` holds the census to the emitter surface on disk.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. FINDINGS REGISTRY
58: 
59: The canonical registry stores open/resolved questions, findings, ruled-out directions, convergence state, and blocked-stop history.
60: 
61: ```json
62: {
63:   "openQuestions": [],
64:   "resolvedQuestions": [],
65:   "keyFindings": [],
66:   "ruledOutDirections": [],
67:   "coverageBySources": {},
68:   "convergenceScore": 0.42,
69:   "blockedStopHistory": [],
70:   "graphConvergenceScore": null,
71:   "graphDecision": null,
72:   "graphBlockers": [],
73:   "lastUpdated": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: Question ownership:
78: 
79: - `inbox.jsonl` is append-only input for external questions.
80: - The registry is the canonical owner of promoted question text, provenance, and operator decisions.
81: - The strategy `key-questions` block is a generated projection and is rewritten from registry state on every reduce step.
82: 
83: When an inbox row targets an existing registry question by promoted question id or inbox id but carries different text, the reducer records a conflict instead of overwriting markdown. Conflict records use `operatorDecision` values of `accepted`, `rejected`, `superseded`, or `needs_decision`; the default unresolved decision is `needs_decision`. The emitted `question_conflict` JSONL event includes both `inboxValue` and `registryValue`.
84: 
85: The reducer writes the registry to `findings-registry.json`; this is the canonical live name. `deep-research-findings-registry.json` is a legacy read-fallback path only -- the reducer checks it when `findings-registry.json` is absent but never writes to it. New docs should reference `findings-registry.json` and mention the legacy name only when explaining read-compatibility.
86: 
87: ---
88: 
89: ## 4. VALIDATION RULES
90: 
91: Blocking validation:
92: 
93: - config, state log, and strategy exist before a resume;
94: - every dispatched iteration produces a non-empty iteration markdown file;
95: - every dispatched iteration appends a JSONL delta record with required fields;
96: - JSONL records parse in strict mode;
97: - reducer-owned outputs refresh after iteration evaluation;
98: - convergence STOP candidates record gate evidence.
99: 
100: Post-dispatch failure codes include:
101: 
102: | Code | Meaning |
103: |------|---------|
104: | `iteration_file_missing` | Expected iteration markdown file was not created |
105: | `iteration_file_empty` | Iteration markdown exists but is empty |
106: | `jsonl_not_appended` | JSONL state did not receive the iteration record |
107: | `jsonl_missing_fields` | Required JSONL fields are absent |
108: | `jsonl_parse_error` | JSONL line is malformed |
109: 
110: Three consecutive failures route to stuck recovery or escalation.
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## 5. FAULT TOLERANCE
115: 
116: Fault-tolerant reads may skip malformed JSONL lines only in lenient recovery mode. Strict mode stops before derived writes.
117: 
118: Safe recovery order:
119: 
120: 1. Preserve the corrupted state file.
121: 2. Read valid JSONL records.
122: 3. Reconstruct missing iteration summaries from `iterations/iteration-NNN.md`.
123: 4. Append explicit reconstructed records.
124: 5. Regenerate registry and dashboard.
125: 6. Record the recovery in JSONL.
126: 
127: Example reconstructed record:
128: 
129: ```json
130: {"type":"iteration","iteration":3,"status":"reconstructed","focus":"extracted focus","findingsCount":0,"newInfoRatio":0.0}
131: ```
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## 6. FILE PROTECTION MAP
136: 
137: The config may include:
138: 
139: ```json
140: {
141:   "fileProtection": {
142:     "deep-research-config.json": "immutable",
143:     "deep-research-state.jsonl": "append-only",
144:     "deep-research-strategy.md": "mutable",
145:     "deep-research-dashboard.md": "auto-generated",
146:     "findings-registry.json": "auto-generated",
147:     "iteration-*.md": "write-once",
148:     "research/research.md": "mutable"
149:   }
150: }
151: ```
152: 
153: Protection is a workflow contract. It documents ownership and supports validation; it is not a substitute for command-level checks.
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## 7. DASHBOARD DERIVATION
158: 
159: Dashboard values are derived from raw state:
160: 
161: | Dashboard Field | Source |
162: |-----------------|--------|
163: | iteration count | JSONL iteration records |
164: | current status | latest lifecycle or synthesis event |
165: | convergence trend | `convergenceSignals` |
166: | blocked stops | registry `blockedStopHistory` |
167: | graph convergence | registry graph fields |
168: | next focus | strategy |
169: 
170: `synthesis_complete` events are authoritative for terminal status when present.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 8. LEGACY ALIASES
175: 
176: The workflow may dual-read older names during migration windows, but new writes use canonical `deep-research-*` artifacts. Migration reads should append a migration event that records `legacyPath`, `canonicalPath`, and timestamp.

33:

38: ## 2. REDUCER CONTRACT
39: 
40: The workflow reducer:
41: 
42: - reads `deep-research-state.jsonl`, per-iteration deltas, strategy, and iteration markdown;
43: - reads `inbox.jsonl` as immutable question input;
44: - reads the prior registry as canonical question state when present;
45: - validates required iteration artifacts;
46: - updates machine-owned strategy sections;
47: - regenerates the findings registry;
48: - regenerates the dashboard;
49: - records convergence and blocked-stop summaries.
50: 
51: It must fail closed before writing derived files when JSONL corruption is detected in strict mode.
52: 
53: Under ledger authority the JSONL it reads is a projection of the ledger, bounded by the registered stems; the registered vocabulary and the producer census are in `state-format.md` section 7, and `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` holds the census to the emitter surface on disk.
54: 
55: ---

57: ## 3. FINDINGS REGISTRY
58: 
59: The canonical registry stores open/resolved questions, findings, ruled-out directions, convergence state, and blocked-stop history.
60: 
61: ```json
62: {
63:   "openQuestions": [],
64:   "resolvedQuestions": [],
65:   "keyFindings": [],
66:   "ruledOutDirections": [],
67:   "coverageBySources": {},
68:   "convergenceScore": 0.42,
69:   "blockedStopHistory": [],
70:   "graphConvergenceScore": null,
71:   "graphDecision": null,
72:   "graphBlockers": [],
73:   "lastUpdated": "2026-05-24T00:00:00Z"
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: Question ownership:
78: 
79: - `inbox.jsonl` is append-only input for external questions.
80: - The registry is the canonical owner of promoted question text, provenance, and operator decisions.
81: - The strategy `key-questions` block is a generated projection and is rewritten from registry state on every reduce step.
82: 
83: When an inbox row targets an existing registry question by promoted question id or inbox id but carries different text, the reducer records a conflict instead of overwriting markdown. Conflict records use `operatorDecision` values of `accepted`, `rejected`, `superseded`, or `needs_decision`; the default unresolved decision is `needs_decision`. The emitted `question_conflict` JSONL event includes both `inboxValue` and `registryValue`.
84: 
85: The reducer writes the registry to `findings-registry.json`; this is the canonical live name. `deep-research-findings-registry.json` is a legacy read-fallback path only -- the reducer checks it when `findings-registry.json` is absent but never writes to it. New docs should reference `findings-registry.json` and mention the legacy name only when explaining read-compatibility.

87: ---

89: ## 4. VALIDATION RULES
90: 
91: Blocking validation:
92: 
93: - config, state log, and strategy exist before a resume;
94: - every dispatched iteration produces a non-empty iteration markdown file;
95: - every dispatched iteration appends a JSONL delta record with required fields;
96: - JSONL records parse in strict mode;
97: - reducer-owned outputs refresh after iteration evaluation;
98: - convergence STOP candidates record gate evidence.
99: 
100: Post-dispatch failure codes include:
101: 
102: | Code | Meaning |
103: |------|---------|
104: | `iteration_file_missing` | Expected iteration markdown file was not created |
105: | `iteration_file_empty` | Iteration markdown exists but is empty |
106: | `jsonl_not_appended` | JSONL state did not receive the iteration record |
107: | `jsonl_missing_fields` | Required JSONL fields are absent |
108: | `jsonl_parse_error` | JSONL line is malformed |
109: 
110: Three consecutive failures route to stuck recovery or escalation.
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## 5. FAULT TOLERANCE
115: 
116: Fault-tolerant reads may skip malformed JSONL lines only in lenient recovery mode. Strict mode stops before derived writes.
117: 
118: Safe recovery order:
119: 
120: 1. Preserve the corrupted state file.
121: 2. Read valid JSONL records.
122: 3. Reconstruct missing iteration summaries from `iterations/iteration-NNN.md`.
123: 4. Append explicit reconstructed records.
124: 5. Regenerate registry and dashboard.
125: 6. Record the recovery in JSONL.
126: 
127: Example reconstructed record:
128: 
129: ```json
130: {"type":"iteration","iteration":3,"status":"reconstructed","focus":"extracted focus","findingsCount":0,"newInfoRatio":0.0}
131: ```

136: 
137: The config may include:
138: 
139: ```json

141:   "fileProtection": {
142:     "deep-research-config.json": "immutable",
143:     "deep-research-state.jsonl": "append-only",
144:     "deep-research-strategy.md": "mutable",
145:     "deep-research-dashboard.md": "auto-generated",

147:     "iteration-*.md": "write-once",
148:     "research/research.md": "mutable"
149:   }
150: }
151: ```
152: 
153: Protection is a workflow contract. It documents ownership and supports validation; it is not a substitute for command-level checks.
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## 7. DASHBOARD DERIVATION
158: 
159: Dashboard values are derived from raw state:
160: 
161: | Dashboard Field | Source |
162: |-----------------|--------|
163: | iteration count | JSONL iteration records |
164: | current status | latest lifecycle or synthesis event |

175:

685: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
686: 
687: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
688: 
689: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
690: 
691: **Decision Criteria**:
692: 
693: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
694: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
695: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
696: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
697: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
698: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
699: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
700: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
701: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
702: 
703: ### Extraction Pattern
704: 
705: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
706: ```markdown
707: ### [Workflow Name]
708: 
709: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
710: 
711: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
712: 
713: **Quick Overview**:
714: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
715: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
716: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
717: 
718: **Configuration Options:**
719: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
720: - Default values optimized for common use cases
721: ```
722: 
723: ### Benefits of Separation
724: 
725: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
726: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
727: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
728: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
729: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
730: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
731: 
732: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
733: 
734: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
735: \```python
736: def detect_mode(request):
737:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
738:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
739:     return 'interactive', 10
740: \```
741: 
742: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
743: 
744: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
745: \```python
746: from dataclasses import dataclass
747: 
748: @dataclass
749: class ModeConfig:
750:     mode: str
751:     depth_rounds: int
752: 
753: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
754:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
755:     if '$quick' in request:
756:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
757:     elif '$ticket' in request:
758:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
759:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
760: \```
761: 
762: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
763: \```python
764: def test_quick_mode():
765:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
766: \```
767: 
768: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
769: 
770: ---
771: 
772: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
773: 
774: ### Purpose
775: 
776: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
777: 
778: **When to use YAML**:
779: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
780: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
781: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
782: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
783: - Validation schemas
784: 
785: ### Standard YAML Structure
786: 
787: ```yaml
788: # [config-name].yaml
789: metadata:
790:   version: "1.0.0"
791:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
792: 
793: config:
794:   threshold_values:
795:     low: 1
796:     medium: 5
797:     high: 10
798:   feature_flags:
799:     enable_feature_x: true
800:   mappings:
801:     $quick: "quick_mode"
802:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
803: ```
804: 
805: ### File Organization
806: 
807: ```
808: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
809: ├── assets/
810: │   ├── workflow-configs/
811: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
812: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
813: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
814: │   ├── mappings/
815: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
816: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
817: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
818: │   └── templates/
819: │       └── [template files]
820: ```
821: 
822: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
823: 
824: ```python
825: import yaml
826: from pathlib import Path
827: 
828: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
829:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
830:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
831:     with open(config_path) as f:
832:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
833: 
834: # Usage
835: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
836: ```
837: 
838: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
839: 
840: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
841: ```markdown
842: | Trigger                    | Action             |
843: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
844: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
845: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
846: ```
847: 
848: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
849: 
850: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
851: ```yaml
852: config:
853:   variant_triggers:
854:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
855:     implicit:
856:       complexity_threshold: 7
857:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
858:   variant_count:
859:     simple: [2, 3]
860:     complex: [5, 10]
861: ```
862: 
863: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
864: ```python
865: import yaml
866: 
867: class VariantDetector:
868:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
869:         with open(config_path) as f:
870:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
871: 
872:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
873:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
874:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
875:             return True
876: 
877:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
878:         if complexity >= threshold:
879:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
880:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
881:         return False
882: ```
883: 
884: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
885: 
886: ---
887: 
888: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
889: 
890: ### When to Use Python for Logic
891: 
892: **Use Python scripts when**:
893: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
894: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
895: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
896: - API integration (external services)
897: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
898: 
899: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
900: 
901: **Always include**:
902: - Type hints for parameters and return values
903: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
904: - Dataclasses for structured data
905: 
906: **Example**:
907: ```python
908: from dataclasses import dataclass
909: from pathlib import Path
910: 
911: @dataclass
912: class ValidationResult:
913:     is_valid: bool
914:     errors: list[str]
915: 
916: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
917:     """
918:     Validate configuration file.
919: 
920:     Args:
921:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
922: 
923:     Returns:
924:         ValidationResult with status and errors
925: 
926:     Raises:
927:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
928:     """
929:     if not config_path.exists():
930:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
931:     # Validation logic
932:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
933: ```
934: 
935: ### Unit Testing Requirements
936: 
937: **Every Python script must have tests**:
938: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
939: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
940: - Framework: pytest
941: 
942: **Example**:
943: ```python
944: import pytest
945: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
946: 
947: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
948:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
949:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
950:     result = validate_config(config)
951:     assert result.is_valid
952: 
953: def test_validate_missing_file():
954:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
955:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
956: ```
957: 
958: ### Import and Reference Patterns
959: 
960: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
961: 
962: **Markdown references**:
963: ```markdown
964: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
965: ```
966: 
967: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
968: 
969: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
970: ```markdown
971: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
972: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
973: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
974: ```
975: 
976: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
977: 
978: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
979: ```python
980: from typing import Literal
981: from dataclasses import dataclass
982: 
983: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
984: 
985: @dataclass
986: class WorkflowDecision:
987:     mode: WorkflowMode
988:     depth_rounds: int
989: 
990: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
991:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
992:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
993:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
994:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
995:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
996:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
997: ```
998: 
999: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
1000: ```python
1001: def test_quick_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1003: 
1004: def test_default_mode():
1005:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1006: ```
1007: 
1008: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1009:

1012: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE

1014: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure

1027: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1028: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1029: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1030: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1031: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1032: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1033: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1034: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1035: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1036: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1037: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1038: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates

1051: 
1052: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**

1054: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests

15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
23: 
24: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
25: 
26: **Core Purpose**:
27: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
28: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
29: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
30: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
31: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
32: 
33: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
34: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
35: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
36: 
37: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
38: 
39: ```
40: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
41:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
42:             ↓
43: Level 2: SKILL.md body
44:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
45:             ↓
46: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
47:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
48: ```
49: 
50: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
51: 
52: ### Location & Naming
53: 
54: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
55: 
56: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
57: 
58: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
59: |---------------|-----------------|
60: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
61: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
62: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
63: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
64: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |

67: 
68: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
69: 
70: ### Title and Intro
71: 
72: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
73: 
74: ```markdown
75: ---
76: title: [Title]
77: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
78: trigger_phrases:
79:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
80:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
81:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
82: importance_tier: normal
83: contextType: general
84: version: 1.0.0.0
85: ---
86: 
87: # [Title]
88: 
89: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: \## 1. OVERVIEW
94: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
95: 
96: ```
97: 
98: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block. The Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal:
99: - 3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content

685: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
686: 
687: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
688: 
689: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
690: 
691: **Decision Criteria**:
692: 
693: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
694: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
695: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
696: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
697: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
698: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
699: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
700: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
701: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
702: 
703: ### Extraction Pattern
704: 
705: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
706: ```markdown
707: ### [Workflow Name]
708: 
709: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
710: 
711: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
712: 
713: **Quick Overview**:
714: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
715: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
716: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
717: 
718: **Configuration Options:**
719: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
720: - Default values optimized for common use cases
721: ```
722: 
723: ### Benefits of Separation
724: 
725: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
726: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
727: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
728: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
729: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
730: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
731: 
732: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
733: 
734: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
735: \```python
736: def detect_mode(request):
737:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
738:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
739:     return 'interactive', 10
740: \```
741: 
742: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
743: 
744: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
745: \```python
746: from dataclasses import dataclass
747: 
748: @dataclass
749: class ModeConfig:
750:     mode: str
751:     depth_rounds: int
752: 
753: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
754:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""

756:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)

758:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
759:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)

762: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
763: \```python
764: def test_quick_mode():
765:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
766: \```
767: 
768: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

838: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
839: 
840: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
841: ```markdown
842: | Trigger                    | Action             |
843: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
844: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
845: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
846: ```
847: 
848: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
849: 
850: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
851: ```yaml
852: config:
853:   variant_triggers:
854:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
855:     implicit:
856:       complexity_threshold: 7
857:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
858:   variant_count:
859:     simple: [2, 3]
860:     complex: [5, 10]
861: ```
862: 
863: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
864: ```python
865: import yaml
866: 
867: class VariantDetector:
868:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
869:         with open(config_path) as f:
870:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
871: 
872:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
873:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
874:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
875:             return True
876: 
877:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
878:         if complexity >= threshold:
879:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
880:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
881:         return False
882: ```
883: 
884: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

888: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
889: 
890: ### When to Use Python for Logic
891: 
892: **Use Python scripts when**:
893: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
894: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
895: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
896: - API integration (external services)
897: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
898: 
899: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
900: 
901: **Always include**:
902: - Type hints for parameters and return values
903: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
904: - Dataclasses for structured data
905: 
906: **Example**:
907: ```python
908: from dataclasses import dataclass
909: from pathlib import Path
910: 
911: @dataclass
912: class ValidationResult:
913:     is_valid: bool
914:     errors: list[str]
915: 
916: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
917:     """
918:     Validate configuration file.
919: 
920:     Args:
921:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
922: 
923:     Returns:
924:         ValidationResult with status and errors
925: 
926:     Raises:
927:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
928:     """
929:     if not config_path.exists():
930:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
931:     # Validation logic
932:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
933: ```
934: 
935: ### Unit Testing Requirements
936: 
937: **Every Python script must have tests**:
938: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
939: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
940: - Framework: pytest
941: 
942: **Example**:
943: ```python
944: import pytest

15: # State Format Reference
16: 
17: Live state packet hub for deep-research files, mutability, and routed state references.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Summarize the live deep-research packet files, mutability rules, and focused state references without carrying every JSON shape inline.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: Load this hub when navigating packet files, deciding file ownership, or choosing which detailed state reference to load next.
30: 
31: ### Routed Details
32: 
33: - `state-jsonl.md` for config, iteration, event, lifecycle, graph, and blocked-stop records.
34: - `state-outputs.md` for strategy, iteration markdown, `research.md`, dashboard, and resource-map output.
35: - `state-reducer-registry.md` for reducer ownership, findings registry, validation, reconstruction, and file protection.
36: 
37: For iterative code review state, use `deep-review`. Review-mode state is not part of this skill's live state contract.
38: 
39: ### Packet Summary
40: 
41: The deep-research loop persists continuity in packet files so each iteration can run with fresh context.
42: 
43: | File | Format | Purpose | Mutability |
44: |------|--------|---------|------------|
45: | `deep-research-config.json` | JSON | Loop parameters and lineage | Created at init; read-only after |
46: | `deep-research-state.jsonl` | JSONL | Append-only structured log | Append-only |
47: | `deep-research-strategy.md` | Markdown | Current research plan and next focus | Reducer-managed sections |
48: | `deep-research-findings-registry.json` / `findings-registry.json` | JSON | Reducer-owned findings and question state | Auto-generated |
49: | `deep-research-dashboard.md` | Markdown | Operator summary | Auto-generated |
50: | `iterations/iteration-NNN.md` | Markdown | Per-iteration narrative | Write-once |
51: | `deltas/iter-NNN.jsonl` | JSONL | Per-iteration structured delta | Write-once |
52: | `research.md` | Markdown | Final/progressive synthesis | Workflow-owned |
53: | `resource-map.md` | Markdown | Optional evidence-derived resource map | Workflow-owned |
54: 
55: The artifact directory is resolved by `resolveArtifactRoot(specFolder, 'research')` from `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/review-research-paths.cjs`.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 2. PACKET LOCATION
60: 
61: Root specs use:
62: 
63: ```text
64: {spec_folder}/research/
65: ```
66: 
67: Child-phase and sub-phase targets use flat-first behavior:
68: 
69: - first run with an empty local `research/` directory writes flat at `{spec_folder}/research/`;
70: - a `{basename(spec_folder)}-pt-NN` subfolder is allocated only when prior content already exists for a non-matching target;
71: - continuation runs reuse the existing matching packet.
72: 
73: This avoids an unnecessary `pt-01` wrapper on first runs.
74: 
75: **Example (first run on a child phase):** `.../026-graph.../019-system-hardening/001-initial-research/004-desc-regen/` writes to `004-desc-regen/research/` directly.
76: 
77: **Example (subsequent run with prior content for a different target):** `004-desc-regen/research/004-desc-regen-pt-02/` (pt-NN allocated as a sibling to the prior content).
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 3. OWNERSHIP MODEL
82: 
83: | Owner | Writes |
84: |-------|--------|
85: | Agent iteration | `iterations/iteration-NNN.md`, JSONL iteration/event append, optional progressive synthesis contribution |
86: | Workflow reducer | strategy machine-owned sections, findings registry, dashboard |
87: | Workflow synthesis | `research.md`, lifecycle snapshots |
88: | Spec anchoring protocol | bounded `spec.md` seed/context/fenced findings block |
89: 
90: The reducer is the source of truth for derived state. Manual edits to reducer-owned outputs are overwritten on the next refresh.
91: 
92: ---
93: 
94: ## 4. FILE PROTECTION
95: 
96: | Protection | Meaning |
97: |------------|---------|
98: | `immutable` | Created once and not modified after init |
99: | `append-only` | New JSONL records may be appended; existing records are not rewritten |
100: | `write-once` | Each iteration artifact is created once |
101: | `mutable` | Workflow may update the file under defined ownership rules |
102: | `auto-generated` | Reducer/workflow regenerates the full file |
103: 
104: The config file carries the protection map; details live in `state-reducer-registry.md`.
105: 
106: ---
107: 
108: ## 5. ROUTED REFERENCES
109: 
110: | Resource | Use When |
111: |----------|----------|
112: | `state-jsonl.md` | Need the JSONL config, iteration, event, lineage, graph, or blocked-stop schemas |
113: | `state-outputs.md` | Need markdown output structure for strategy, iterations, dashboard, research synthesis, or resource map |
114: | `state-reducer-registry.md` | Need reducer ownership, registry schema, validation, fault tolerance, or reconstruction |
115: | `../convergence/convergence.md` | Need STOP contract and legal-stop semantics |
116: | `../protocol/spec-check-protocol.md` | Need bounded `spec.md` anchoring and generated-fence write-back |
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ## 6. NON-GOALS
121: 
122: - Do not document `deep-review` state here; route to the sibling skill.
123: - Do not treat legacy aliases as write targets. The workflow reads legacy aliases only for migration windows and writes canonical `deep-research-*` names.
124: - Do not manually edit reducer-owned dashboard or registry files.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 7. LEDGER VOCABULARY AND PROJECTION CEILING
129: 
130: ### Registered vocabulary
131: 
132: The canonical dotted stems for this mode live in `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-research-ledger-schema/deep-research-ledger-types.ts`:
133: 
134: - `DeepResearchEventStems` — the registered stems the ledger accepts.
135: - `DEEP_RESEARCH_STEM_PRODUCERS` — one entry per stem recording whether a mechanical producer emits it today (`spoken`, with the producer files) or why nothing does (`reserved`).
136: 
137: `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` scans the workflow assets and runtime scripts and fails (exit 2) when a registered stem has no producer, a spoken stem has no emitter, or a reserved stem is emitted anyway.
138: 
139: ### Which file is authoritative
140: 
141: `deep-research-state.jsonl` is authoritative while the mode's authority record (`authority-deep-research.json`, state `legacy_authoritative`) names the legacy writer. Once the record moves to `new_authoritative_reversible` or `new_authoritative_final` with `selectedWriter: "dark"`, the ledger is authoritative and the append gateway refreshes this file as a projection after each append.
142: 
143: ### What a projection refresh can reproduce
144: 
145: The projection folds only registered stems, and its `run_initialized` arm rebuilds a thin config row: `type`, `topic`, `maxIterations`, `generation`, `timestamp`. A pre-flip config row written by the workflow carries more — `convergenceThreshold`, `minIterations`, `minIdeaObservations`, `antiConvergence`, `sessionId`, `executor`, `specFolder`, `createdAt` — and a refresh cannot rebuild those keys.
146: 
147: Because losing them silently would look like a complete projection, a replace that would drop keys from an existing `type: "config"` first row is refused with `ATTRIBUTION_COLLAPSE` (invariant `no-attribution-loss-on-replace`) before any bytes are written. An operator who hits it either migrates the attribution into a registered `deep_research.run_initialized` payload or moves the legacy file aside to accept the loss deliberately.

59: ## 2. PACKET LOCATION

128: ## 7. LEDGER VOCABULARY AND PROJECTION CEILING
129: 
130: ### Registered vocabulary
131: 
132: The canonical dotted stems for this mode live in `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-research-ledger-schema/deep-research-ledger-types.ts`:
133: 
134: - `DeepResearchEventStems` — the registered stems the ledger accepts.
135: - `DEEP_RESEARCH_STEM_PRODUCERS` — one entry per stem recording whether a mechanical producer emits it today (`spoken`, with the producer files) or why nothing does (`reserved`).
136: 
137: `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` scans the workflow assets and runtime scripts and fails (exit 2) when a registered stem has no producer, a spoken stem has no emitter, or a reserved stem is emitted anyway.
138: 
139: ### Which file is authoritative
140: 
141: `deep-research-state.jsonl` is authoritative while the mode's authority record (`authority-deep-research.json`, state `legacy_authoritative`) names the legacy writer. Once the record moves to `new_authoritative_reversible` or `new_authoritative_final` with `selectedWriter: "dark"`, the ledger is authoritative and the append gateway refreshes this file as a projection after each append.
142: 
143: ### What a projection refresh can reproduce
144: 
145: The projection folds only registered stems, and its `run_initialized` arm rebuilds a thin config row: `type`, `topic`, `maxIterations`, `generation`, `timestamp`. A pre-flip config row written by the workflow carries more — `convergenceThreshold`, `minIterations`, `minIdeaObservations`, `antiConvergence`, `sessionId`, `executor`, `specFolder`, `createdAt` — and a refresh cannot rebuild those keys.
146: 
147: Because losing them silently would look like a complete projection, a replace that would drop keys from an existing `type: "config"` first row is refused with `ATTRIBUTION_COLLAPSE` (invariant `no-attribution-loss-on-replace`) before any bytes are written. An operator who hits it either migrates the attribution into a registered `deep_research.run_initialized` payload or moves the legacy file aside to accept the loss deliberately.

# Deep Review State Reducer And Registry

The reducer is the single writer for derived review state. Iteration agents append evidence; the reducer reconciles it into registry, dashboard, and strategy views.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

The reducer turns append-only review evidence into the current findings registry, dashboard, and strategy state. It is the authority for derived outputs, not a second source of truth.

---

## 2. OWNERSHIP

| Surface | Writer | Rule |
|---------|--------|------|
| JSONL state | Workflow plus validated iteration append | Append-only |
| Findings registry | `scripts/reduce-state.cjs` | Regenerate from JSONL |
| Dashboard | `scripts/reduce-state.cjs` | Regenerate from registry and latest events |
| Strategy machine sections | `scripts/reduce-state.cjs` | Update from coverage and findings |
| Iteration markdown | Review iteration agent | Write-once |
| Review report | Synthesis | Final handoff |

No agent should hand-edit reducer-owned derived state as the authoritative fix. Repair JSONL or rerun the reducer.

Under ledger authority the JSONL the reducer reads is a projection of the ledger, bounded by the registered stems; the registered vocabulary and the producer census are in `state-format.md` section 11, and `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/check-ledger-stem-producers.cjs` holds the census to the emitter surface on disk.

---

## 3. FINDINGS REGISTRY

The registry groups findings into:

- Active findings.
- Resolved findings.
- Repeated findings.
- Blocked or disputed findings.
- Claim-adjudicated severity changes.

Each active finding needs severity, category, file:line evidence, finding class, content hash, first-seen iteration, and latest-seen iteration.

---

## 4. FAIL-CLOSED BEHAVIOR

The reducer must refuse to publish derived state when JSONL is corrupt in strict mode. That protects dashboards and verdict previews from silently losing findings.
